translations.answer: The method avoids joint-torque sensors by estimating torque from position-servo error and feeding it to TSID. It still uses wrist/ankle six-axis force sensors, an IMU, and encoders, while the paper's experiments cover only six joints of HRP-2's right leg in controlled free-motion and contact settings. It is therefore neither sensorless nor a plug-and-play cross-platform whole-body torque controller.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The mapping from position error to torque for each high-ratio joint has been identified on the target hardware.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Wrist/ankle force sensors, encoders, and the IMU remain available and calibrated.
translations.applicability.controllers.0: Position-interface torque estimation and Task-Space Inverse Dynamics (TSID)
translations.applicability.environments.0: Controlled HRP-2 single-leg free motion and rigid-contact experiments
translations.applicability.robots.0: HRP-2; transfer to another actuator requires new identification
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper provides a detailed identification derivation and HRP-2 experiments, while public TSID code supports inspection of the inverse-dynamics layer. Tests cover only six right-leg joints and still rely on wrist/ankle F/T sensing, an IMU, and encoders; the repository does not reproduce the complete actuator-identification pipeline.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Chapters 2-5, Figures 3-12, and the experimental appendix
translations.evidence.0.note: Derives position-error torque estimation, friction compensation, and TSID task constraints, then evaluates them in bounded HRP-2 settings.
translations.evidence.0.title: Implementing Torque Control with High-Ratio Gear Boxes and without Joint-Torque Sensors
